title: the WSG consuming and carrying food and Table 33 slice - the ration ladder, the spoilage mechanics and Table 33: chance of food spoilage, printed p. 58
audit_label: R466 WSG food carrying pin audit
audit_comment: The Table 33 spoilage grid cell by cell (the max days and the pct per food type per temperature band), the ration ladder (the fish half ration, the size S/M/L rations, the twenty-ration butchering) and the spoilage mechanics (the warmest-category rule, the ratchet, the frozen and thaw rules, the taint and spoil CON modifiers and penalties, the ration-value chance) - every cell, const and bool verified against the model.

banner.title: R466: the WSG CONSUMING AND CARRYING FOOD slice - the ration ladder (one fish half a ration, one size S animal a full ration, one size M animal feeding three characters for a day, one size L animal six rations, at least twenty rations for a full day of expert butchering), the druid disapproval of intentional overkill with the feed-three excuse, carrying the excess subject only to encumbrance and spoilage, and Table 33: the food spoilage grid by effective temperature with the taint and spoil mechanics, printed p. 58.
banner.provenance: Ground truth two-way: the pdfy embedded OCR text layer of the printed p. 58 content stream (the FlateDecode stream of pageobj 549, decompressed and position-read) vs the djvu word layer (Guide_0058), with the arithmetic ladders as the tiebreaker. Both layers agree on every Table 33 value cell except the green-plants 31-50 cell, where the pdfy reads 6/20 against a djvu garble; 6/20 fits the clean days ladder (6, 4, 2, 1) and the pct ladder (20, 30, 40, 50). The below-30 column is a dash in every row (both layers garble the dash glyph); the book explanation sentence - spoilage will not occur as long as the effective temperature remains within this range - confirms the dash, and continually frozen food keeps indefinitely no matter how long it is carried. The printed p. 58 image shows scanner double-imaging (a ghost copy about 12 pixels below the true print) which defeated the pixel and vision reads; the text layers carry the table. The mechanics: the effective temperature is the warmest category applying at least one hour that day, a category once used ratchets to the same or warmer for all later checks, thawed food is subject to spoilage from the thaw day (counted as day 1) even if promptly re-frozen; one failed check taints (a secret Wisdom Check to notice, eatable anyway, a CON check at +4 to avoid nausea and cramps within 1d10+10 minutes, a -1 penalty on attacks and dodging or maneuvering saves for 12 hours, then an unmodified CON check per hour to recover, tainted food still a full ration); a second failed check obviously spoils (CON check at +10, penalties at least 24 hours if stricken, else a 50% chance the food still provides the full or half ration value, otherwise no nourishment at all). The onset window is 11-20 minutes (1d10+10). The gluttony and indigestion note: the rules do not account for them.
banner.sentinel: All 40 Table 33 cells pinned (the max days and the spoilage pct per food type per temperature band); the ration ladder and the taint and spoil mechanics are audit examples, including the dash column and the frozen and thaw rules.

consts.name: wccRowCount
consts.comment: the Table 33 row count: green plants, fruits or vegetables, cooked meat, raw meat

consts.name: wccFishRationNum
consts.comment: one fish provides half of a character minimum daily ration: the numerator

consts.name: wccFishRationDen
consts.comment: the fish half-ration denominator

consts.name: wccSizeSRations
consts.comment: one size S animal is one full ration

consts.name: wccSizeMFeedCount
consts.comment: one size M animal is enough to feed three characters for one day

consts.name: wccSizeLRations
consts.comment: one size L animal is six rations worth of food

consts.name: wccButcherRations
consts.comment: at least twenty full rations from a size L carcass with expert butchering

consts.name: wccButcherDays
consts.comment: the expert butchering takes one full day of butchering, slicing and packaging

consts.name: wccOverkillFeedCount
consts.comment: killing one size L animal to feed himself and two others is an excusable overkill

consts.name: wccTempHourGate
consts.comment: a temperature category applies as the effective temperature only if it held for at least one hour on that day

consts.name: wccThawStartDay
consts.comment: thawed food is subject to spoilage beginning on the thaw day, counting that day as day 1

consts.name: wccTaintConMod
consts.comment: eating tainted food demands a Constitution check with a +4 modifier to avoid suffering

consts.name: wccTaintOnsetDie
consts.comment: the tainted-food onset die: 1d10

consts.name: wccTaintOnsetBase
consts.comment: the tainted-food onset base: nausea and cramps within 1d10+10, the 11-20 minute window

consts.name: wccTaintAtkPenalty
consts.comment: the tainted-food penalty: -1 on all attack rolls and on dodging or maneuvering saves

consts.name: wccTaintPenaltyHours
consts.comment: the tainted-food penalty lasts for 12 hours

consts.name: wccTaintRecheckMins
consts.comment: after the 12 hours, recovery checks come at one per hour until one succeeds

consts.name: wccSpoilConMod
consts.comment: eating spoiled food demands a Constitution check with a +10 modifier to avoid the illness

consts.name: wccSpoilPenaltyHours
consts.comment: if stricken by spoiled food, the penalties last at least 24 hours instead of 12

consts.name: wccSpoilRationPct
consts.comment: if spoiled food causes no illness, a 50% chance it still provides the full ration value (or half, if only that much was eaten)

bools.name: wccGluttonyNotModeled
bools.comment: these rules do not account for gluttony or indigestion - that is left to the Dungeon Master

bools.name: wccDruidDisapprovesOverkill
bools.comment: a druid in the party strongly disapproves if hunters or fishermen intentionally kill more than they can conceivably eat in one sitting

bools.name: wccOverkillExcusable
bools.comment: an overkill cannot always be helped: the hunter feeding three is not held responsible for the leftovers

bools.name: wccExcessCarryAllowed
bools.comment: excess food need not be left behind when the party breaks camp - it can be carried along

bools.name: wccEncumbranceDMCall
bools.comment: encumbrance, the first of the two carrying factors, is a Dungeon Master ruling

bools.name: wccDashNoSpoilage
bools.comment: the Table 33 dash: spoilage will not occur as long as the effective temperature remains within the below-30 range

bools.name: wccFrozenKeepsIndefinitely
bools.comment: food kept continually frozen will be good to eat no matter how long it is carried or stored

bools.name: wccThawSpoilsEvenIfRefrozen
bools.comment: thawed food is subject to spoilage from the thaw day even if promptly re-frozen after the exposure

bools.name: wccWarmestCategoryApplies
bools.comment: the effective temperature is the warmest category that applied on the given day, gated by the one-hour rule

bools.name: wccCategoryRatchet
bools.comment: once a temperature category is used for one spoilage check, the same or a warmer one is used for all subsequent checks

bools.name: wccOneFailTainted
bools.comment: food that fails one spoilage check is tainted - not as good as fresh, but not obviously spoiled

bools.name: wccTaintSecretWisdomCheck
bools.comment: a character intending to eat tainted food gets a secret Wisdom Check to notice the spoilage first

bools.name: wccMayEatAnyway
bools.comment: a character who notices the taint may choose to eat the food anyway

bools.name: wccTwoFailsSpoiled
bools.comment: food that fails a second spoilage check is obviously spoiled and perceived as such by anyone intending to eat it

bools.name: wccTaintFullRationValue
bools.comment: tainted food still provides a normal amount of food value: a full ration still counts as a full ration

bools.name: wccSpoiledHalfRationIfHalfEaten
bools.comment: if only half of the no-illness spoiled food was eaten, it counts as a half-ration

bools.name: wccSpoiledNoNourishment
bools.comment: otherwise the spoiled food is so spoiled it does not serve as nourishment - as if not eaten at all
